label: H.R. 6291

latest_action.text: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by the Yeas and Nays: 14 - 10.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 6291 amends the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 to expand online privacy protections to include teens (defined as individuals over 12 and under 17 years old). It regulates how commercial websites, online services, online applications, and mobile applications collect, use, disclose, and store personal information from children and teens, prohibiting targeted advertising to these groups and setting up new rights for parents and teens to access, correct, and delete data.

affected_groups.effect: Individuals aged 16 and under receive protections against targeted advertising, enhanced rights to delete or correct personal data, and stricter limitations on online data collection.
Parents of children receive expanded rights to review, delete, and control the collection of their children's personal information online.

Commercial operators of websites, online services, and mobile applications must comply with new consent mechanisms, data retention limits, storage disclosure rules, and bans on targeted advertising to minors.
Large social media companies generating high revenues and user counts face specific oversight reports by the FTC regarding compliance.

key_provisions: Expands privacy protections and data collection rules under the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act to cover teens aged 13 through 16.
Prohibits operators from collecting, using, disclosing, or maintaining personal information from children or teens for the purpose of providing individual-specific advertising.

Requires operators to provide clear and conspicuous notice of information practices and obtain verifiable consent from parents of children or directly from teens before material changes to data practices.
Grants teens and parents of children or teens the right to access, review, correct, and delete personal information and content submitted to websites or applications.
Imposes restrictions on storing or transferring personal information in covered nations without proper notice.
Preempts state laws related to the provisions of the Act, establishing a uniform federal standard.
Directs the Federal Trade Commission to submit reports on enforcement actions and investigate processes used by high-impact social media companies.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 6291 amends the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 to expand online privacy protections to include teens (defined as individuals over 12 and under 17 years old). It regulates how commercial websites, online services, online applications, and mobile applications collect, use, disclose, and store personal information from children and teens, prohibiting targeted advertising to these groups and setting up new rights for parents and teens to access, correct, and delete data.
summary_detail.significance: H.R. 6291 significantly updates federal privacy law by extending legal protections previously reserved for children to teenagers. By banning individualized targeted advertising for minors and establishing comprehensive rights for data deletion and correction across websites and mobile applications, the bill alters how digital platforms interact with young users and manage their data.
